extracted.intended_audience: Users, developers, and researchers of the Isabelle proof assistant (people installing, running, or contributing to Isabelle)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and release/installation guidance for the Isabelle proof assistant, including hardware requirements, supported platforms, notable changes, distribution/licensing, and support channels. Aimed at people preparing to install or use Isabelle and those tracking changes between releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardware requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Small experiments: 4 GB memory, 2 CPU cores; Medium applications: 8 GB memory, 4 CPU cores; Large projects: 16 GB memory, 8 CPU cores; Extra-large projects: 64 GB memory, 16 CPU cores
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these tiers to choose appropriate hardware for the expected scale of Isabelle workloads; larger projects require substantially more memory and cores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported platforms / downloads
rubrics_metrics.description: Now available: Isabelle2025-2 (January 2026). Download for Linux (Intel), Download for Linux (ARM), Download for Windows, Download for macOS
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the correct platform-specific installer for your OS and CPU architecture. The page lists distinct downloads for Intel and ARM Linux builds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release compatibility and notes
rubrics_metrics.description: This version supersedes Isabelle2025-1, see the NEWS file for further details. Isabelle2025-1 and Isabelle2025-2 use the same version of the Archive of Formal Proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the NEWS file for detailed change notes and verify Archive of Formal Proofs compatibility when migrating between releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Isabelle is distributed for free under a conglomerate of open-source licenses, but the main code-base is subject to BSD-style regulations. The application bundles include source and binary packages and documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of mixed open-source licenses; review the bundled source and binary packages and the installation instructions for licensing details before redistribution or integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support channels and subscription recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Support is available by the official documentation and mailing lists: The isabelle-users mailing list provides a forum for Isabelle users to discuss problems, exchange information, and make announcements. The isabelle-dev mailing list covers the Isabelle development process. Zulip Chat is a real-time discussion platform with a minimalistic public archive. Stack Overflow and Stack Exchange are Q&A platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users of official releases should subscribe to isabelle-users; developers or those using development snapshots should subscribe to isabelle-dev. Use Zulip for real-time discussion and Stack Exchange for Q&A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor (Isabelle/jEdit) features & accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Isabelle/jEdit: support for dark mode and screen readers; built-in navigator, without requiring plugins; more reactive mouse handling (notably on macOS); updated FlatLaf GUI L&F with scalable SVG icons; improved appearance on Linux (GUI scaling) and macOS (L&F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor usability and accessibility improvements (dark mode, screen reader support, navigator, GUI scaling and icons) are part of the release — relevant for desktop users and those requiring accessibility features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor (Isabelle/VSCode) improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Isabelle/VSCode: more robust session build process on console; GUI panels for Documentation, Symbols, Sledgehammer; update of underlying VSCodium distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VSCode integration enhancements aim to improve session builds and provide integrated panels for common tasks; update your VSCodium-based distribution to receive these improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: System tools and command-line behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: System: ML settings may depend on command-line system options (-o). System: command-line tool to process theories within adhoc session. System: more detailed build progress. System: more robust build cluster management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that ML settings and build behavior can be affected by command-line options; use the provided command-line tools and updated build progress/cluster management features for large or automated builds.

rubrics_metrics.name: HOL library and tooling improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: HOL: various improvements of theory libraries. HOL: various improvements to code generation. HOL: updates and improvements of Sledgehammer and external provers. HOL: generation of running time functions for HOL functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes affect users of the HOL logic and code generation; review library and toolchain updates (including Sledgehammer/external provers) when upgrading to ensure proofs and generated code behave as expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive of Formal Proofs availability
rubrics_metrics.description: A vast collection of Isabelle examples and applications is available from the Archive of Formal Proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Archive as a resource for examples, libraries, and applications; check compatibility notes in release documentation regarding the Archive version.
